claims.text: High-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings contain chemically and structurally distinct interfaces.
Well-defined interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Interface-mediated obstruction of dislocations delays creep onset relative to homogeneous coatings.
Interface-mediated obstruction of dislocations reduces creep rate relative to homogeneous coatings.
The proposed multilayer coating has distinct compositional layers and sharp interfaces.
The controlled comparison should use multilayer and monolithic high-entropy-alloy coatings with the same overall composition.
The comparison should be conducted under constant load at moderate temperatures and stresses.
Dislocation-based plasticity is the dominant deformation mode within the proposed test regime.
Chemically and structurally distinct interfaces impede dislocation nucleation.
Chemically and structurally distinct interfaces impede dislocation propagation.
Interfaces pin and block dislocations and create localized stress fields.
Localized interface-associated stress fields delay plastic deformation.
Blocking dislocation motion at interfaces limits creep-strain accumulation relative to coatings without engineered interfaces.
Under identical constant-load conditions, multilayer coatings will have a significantly lower creep-strain rate than compositionally equivalent monolithic coatings.
Under identical constant-load conditions, multilayer coatings will show a delayed onset of plastic deformation relative to compositionally equivalent monolithic coatings.
The proposed mechanism requires interfaces to retain their quality with minimal interdiffusion.
Extreme temperatures or other conditions that degrade interfaces may invalidate the mechanism.
Dislocation accumulation at interfaces, observable by TEM, would provide microstructural evidence of the proposed barrier effect.
Failure to observe a statistically significant reduction in creep-strain rate or delay in plastic-deformation onset would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe an interfacial barrier effect in post-deformation microstructural analysis would falsify the hypothesis.
